title: Locality Sensitive Hashing for Optimizing Subgraph Query Processing in Parallel Computing Systems

problem.claim: Efficient subgraph query processing is needed for large graphs in parallel computing systems.

gap.claim: Widely used hash-based methods do not exploit locality-sensitive hashing for the stated intraquery and interquery optimization goals.

contributions.claim: QCMH uses data-graph and subgraph-query structures to merge multiple tasks during a single subgraph query.
QMH detects common subgraphs among different subgraph queries to merge multiple queries.
The proposed locality-sensitive hashing methods target redundant computation across tasks within one query and across multiple queries.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on large real and synthetic graphs reportedly show 10% to 50% query-performance improvement over state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper addresses efficient subgraph query processing in large graphs using parallel computing systems.
It aims to exploit intraquery and interquery parallelism.
It extends locality-sensitive hashing and introduces QCMH for merging tasks within a query and QMH for merging related queries.
The methods are intended to reduce redundant computation.
Experiments on large real and synthetic graphs report 10% to 50% better query performance than state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The approach merges tasks or queries that share exploitable structure.

interpretation.claim: Identifying common structure can reduce duplicated computation in parallel graph-query workloads.

application.claim: For related graph queries, consider structure-aware grouping before executing parallel tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach benefits workloads without sufficient structural overlap.

unknowns: Algorithmic details and implementation requirements are not provided.
Datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, and experimental protocol are not specified.
The abstract does not report limits, overheads, or workload conditions for the claimed improvements.
